title: Quick check: Designing Context Providers

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Designing Context Providers”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Provider placement should have clear ownership and avoid duplicated or contradictory state.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Provider placement should have clear ownership and avoid duplicated or contradictory state.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Designing Context Providers: Provider placement should have clear ownership and avoid duplicated or contradictory state.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Provider placement?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Choose one source of truth and avoid storing values that can be computed from existing state.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Choose one source of truth and avoid storing values that can be computed from existing state.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Designing Context Providers: Choose one source of truth and avoid storing values that can be computed from existing state.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Designing Context Providers” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Designing Context Providers: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
